title: Bangladesh Bank doubles concessional loan scheme to $120 mn
summary:
Bangladesh Bank has doubled its refinancing scheme to Tk1,500 crore ($120 million) to provide affordable loans to marginalised groups, small businesses and students.
Commercial banks can access funds at 1 per cent interest and lend at up to 7 per cent. 
At least 25 per cent of disbursements must benefit women borrowers and entrepreneurs.

title: EU to boost free carbon allowances for energy-intensive industries
summary:
The EU has agreed to provide around 121 million free carbon allowances to energy-intensive industries from 2026 to 2030, aiming to protect competitiveness and prevent carbon leakage. 
The deal includes targeted support for vulnerable sectors, with unused allowances channelled into modernisation and innovation funds. 
It awaits formal approval by the Council and European Parliament.

title: EU generated 2.3 mn tonnes of textile waste in 2024: Eurostat
summary:
EU textile waste reached 2.3 million tonnes in 2024, with household disposal accounting for more than half, Eurostat data showed.
The EU treated 1.4 million tonnes, or 63 per cent of generated textile waste; 91 per cent of treated textiles went to recovery operations.
Italy led generation at 441,736 tonnes and treatment at 280,680 tonnes.

title: Geoeconomic shifts threaten developing countries' growth: UNCTAD
summary:
UNCTAD warns that geoeconomic shifts are weakening developing countries’ growth prospects, with global growth projected to slow to 2.6 per cent in 2026. 
Strategic investment, trade and technology are increasingly concentrated in developed economies, while volatile finance and declining aid add pressure. 
The report calls for stronger industrial policies, regional cooperation and productive capacity.

title: Syre’s $1 bn Vietnam plan: Can textile-to-textile recycling scale?
summary:
Syre is reviewing its $1 billion Vietnam recycled polyester project, while still envisaging a 150,000-tonne facility.
The Nhon Hoi project received an investment certificate in June 2025 and was announced with 250,000 tonnes of annual output.
Feedstock needs of 300,000-400,000 tonnes exceed expected domestic discarded-fabric supply; Vietnam’s permitted-scrap list does not list textile waste.

title: Is viscose staple fibre gaining strength as pulp holds flat?
summary:
China’s viscose staple fibre market firmed in fine-denier grades between November 4 and 11, with 1.2D×38mm VSF rising 2.0 per cent and 1.5D×38mm gaining 1.4 per cent.
The grades closed at $2.256/kg and $2.234/kg respectively after a mid-week step-up, while wood pulp stayed near $0.950/kg.
High-end and medium grades were unchanged, showing specification-led demand rather than a broad rally.

title: South India cotton yarn prices stable, post-Diwali demand weak
summary:
Mumbai and Tiruppur cotton yarn prices stayed stable as post-Diwali buyers delayed purchases and downstream units remained below normal operations.
Tight payment flows kept trade thin across the textile value chain, while traders expect buying and replenishment to improve next week.
Gujarat cotton prices were unchanged on lower kapas arrivals; all-India arrivals were put at 80,000–82,000 bales.

title: Uzbekistan's $400 mn cotton cluster: Can it become Europe's next hub?
summary:
Uzbekistan plans a $400 million cotton-to-textile cluster in Romitan, Bukhara, adding a sourcing base near European and CIS markets.
It is part of Bukhara’s 145-project, $7.8 billion programme, with 9,000 hectares proposed and a 65 per cent high-value output target.
Lihua Group is partner, but ownership, input traceability and renewable power supply need verification under EU and US rules.

title: 29 Bhiwandi textile units face MPCB notices: Is fabric supply at risk?
summary:
Grey-fabric buyers and yarn suppliers should review exposure after Bhiwandi’s sizing association reportedly suspended operations from November 8.
It cited weak markets, higher raw-material costs, skilled-worker shortages, rising wages and compliance expenses.
Scope remains unconfirmed; MPCB notices were reported for 22 sizing and 7 dyeing units, while MMF GST cuts were not the trigger.

title: Bata India chases younger consumers with sneakers and premium lines
summary:
Bata India is targeting younger consumers through sneakers, premium lines and consumer-led stores to sustain sales growth.
Quarterly turnover grew 7.5 per cent to ₹861.8 crore (~$91.6 million), as higher price points lifted prices and footfall.
Franchisee, institutional and distribution channels grew double digits; e-commerce grew and adjusted profit before tax rose over 31 per cent.

title: Cambodia’s apparel exports reach at $10 bn in January-October 2026
summary:
Cambodia’s apparel exports rose 6.31 per cent YoY to $10.223 billion in January–October 2026, remaining the country’s largest export earner.
Shipments made up 34.1 per cent of total merchandise exports, with knitted apparel up 4.3 per cent and non-knitted apparel up 10.9 per cent.
Cotton and cotton yarn imports surged 29.5 per cent, signalling stronger demand for cotton-based manufacturing.

title: Bangladesh's garment factories shut amid protests over wage hike
summary:
Wage protests have halted more than 100 garment factories in Gazipur, Ashulia and Savar, with 11 units announcing indefinite closures ahead of Bangladesh's minimum wage talks.
Workers proposed Tk32,000 (~$256) a month, while employers may submit a proposal but boycott Monday's Minimum Wage Board meeting.
RMG accounts for around 80 per cent of Bangladesh's $48 billion in annual exports.

title: 5.4% of US importers face a new customs rule: What changes in 2027?
summary:
US apparel companies under DDP terms should review import arrangements before CBP's foreign-IOR rule takes effect on January 5, 2027.
Foreign IORs must be CTPAT-validated or use a CTPAT-validated licensed broker, which must act as IOR when the principal is not owner or purchaser.
CBP cited $1.16 billion in unpaid foreign-IOR duties from 2020 to August 2026, with only $35.7 million collected.

title: US’ Wolverine posts eighth consecutive quarter of growth in Q3 FY26
summary:
Wolverine World Wide has raised its FY26 outlook after third-quarter revenue rose 7.5 per cent to $505.4 million and net earnings attributable to the company reached $65.8 million.
Operating margin expanded to 17.7 per cent, aided by $35.3 million in IEEPA tariff refunds.
The footwear and apparel group now expects FY26 revenue of $2.00-$2.01 billion and adjusted diluted EPS of $1.95-$1.99.

title: India's $1 bn US apparel gap: Can exporters win back buyers?
summary:
TexPro found India's US apparel imports fell $1.014 billion in January-August 2026, down 25.96 per cent as the market slipped 7.02 per cent.
Its share fell to 5.59 per cent from 7.02 per cent, while Vietnam and Cambodia gained and knitted apparel led losses.
Talks may ease clearance, but no apparel-specific tariff relief is confirmed; recovery hinges on price, delivery and policy stability.

title: US' AAFA welcomes Senate passage of Customs Notification Act
summary:
AAFA has welcomed US Senate passage of the Customs Notification Act (H.R. 4930), saying it would strengthen CBP’s ability to share information with brands and stakeholders. 
The measure covers products, packaging and packing materials linked to suspected counterfeit shipments during IP enforcement. 
AAFA president and CEO Steve Lamar urged President Trump to sign it into law.

title: Japan's Mizuno reports 9.9% H1 sales growth, retains FY27 outlook
summary:
Japanese sporting goods company Mizuno Corporation reported record first-half FY27 results, with net sales rising 9.9 per cent to ~$871.96 million and operating profit increasing 22.1 per cent. 
Growth was driven by strong demand for Football, Golf, Running and Sportstyle products, particularly in Europe and the Americas. 
The company maintained its full-year forecast, targeting 8.1 per cent sales growth.

title: Canada's 14-year tariff plan: Can Indonesia win more apparel orders?
summary:
Indonesia’s apparel share in Canada rose to 3.35 per cent in January-August 2026 as its shipments slipped 0.6 per cent while Canada’s total apparel imports fell 7.3 per cent.
TexPro says knitted imports from Indonesia grew 6.6 per cent to $132.94 million, while woven apparel dropped 8.1 per cent to $109.52 million.
CEPA starts on December 1, 2026, with duty cuts and fabric-origin flexibility.

title: Bangladesh's RMG exports to EU rise 2.79% in July-October
summary:
Bangladesh's ready-made garment exports to the EU rose 2.79 per cent year-on-year to $6.43 billion in July-October of fiscal 2026-27, EPB data showed.
Spain led with $1.448 billion and Germany followed with $1.439 billion; the top five EU markets accounted for two-thirds of exports.
October exports to the bloc increased 1.10 per cent to $1.53 billion.

title: Sri Lanka's €744 mn EU trade: Can GSP+ survive the 2028 test?
summary:
Sri Lanka plans to reapply for EU GSP+ under the 2027 to 2036 framework, with preferences running until December 31, 2028 during transition.
Only 57.3 per cent of eligible Sri Lankan clothing imports used GSP+ in 2024, leaving €554 million outside the scheme.
Apparel exports fell 5.52 per cent in January to September 2026, while compliance, origin rules and sourcing flexibility shape renewal risks.
